start_here: Say to your AI: "Record my AI tokens from my Claude Code transcripts now." It reads the saved byte cursors, reads only the new transcript lines with tool:record-ai-work-tokens, and runs the SQL it returns with tool:run-sql-in-my-database against the database that holds claude_messages.
no_lists_because: This item keeps no list the person edits: it writes two measurement tables, claude_messages (one row per assistant message with its token usage) and transcript_cursors (the byte offset read in each transcript file), both named in its SQL plan, not in a list.
instructions: 1. Make sure the database named in your store holds the tables claude_messages and transcript_cursors (the SQL plan creates no tables; the measurement tables must already exist).
2. Say "Record my AI tokens from my Claude Code transcripts now." Your AI reads transcript_cursors, which is empty on the first run, so every transcript is read once.
3. Run the SQL the tool returns with tool:run-sql-in-my-database. Read the stats it gives back: files_seen, files_read, assistant_records, bad_line and partial_only.
4. Repeat on the next day; only the lines written since the saved cursors are read again.
